name: Executive order of March 25, 1874 setting apart the San Juan reservation for the Jicarilla Apache
promises: Not a treaty. The President withdrew from sale and settlement, subject to action by Congress, the tract described in the agreement of December 10, 1873: from the San Juan River where it crosses the southern line of Colorado, along the river to the Navajo reservation, north to Colorado and east to the start.
today: The President cancelled this order on July 18, 1876 and restored the land to the public domain. The Indian Claims Commission found (Docket 22-A, 1963) that the Jicarilla refused to go to this reserve, and that their aboriginal title was taken gradually without payment; the land claim was settled for $9,150,000 in 1971.

openQuestions: Under the 2026-11-08 rule the 1876 cancellation of this executive-order reserve is not by itself a breach; it has its own record (cession-1876-07-18-apache-jicarilla-bands).
The Commission's Finding 54 places this reserve "in Colorado"; Royce and the order place it in New Mexico Territory south of the Colorado line. Left unresolved.
Where the Docket 22-A gradual-taking finding should be counted is unsettled; it is not counted here.
